speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about the shooting ear pain you are experiencing and how long it has been since your tympanoplasty?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any clicking sounds or a sensation of fullness in the right ear when you chew or move your jaw? I also need to know if the pain is localized specifically around the tragus or the ear canal entrance.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of teeth grinding or jaw clicking, and does pressing on the area in front of your ear reproduce the pain? I also need to know if the pain is sharp and localized to the tragus or if it feels deeper within the ear canal.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. Underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks prior. Social history: Works as a cashier at a local department store.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient's symptoms of shooting pain with eating and earring discomfort, combined with stress and poor sleep, suggest temporomandibular joint dysfunction or myofascial pain rather than a surgical complication. I will request an examination of the temporomandibular joint and surrounding musculature to confirm tenderness and range of motion. REQUEST TEST: TMJ_Exam

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the TMJ examination is normal, I need to rule out neuralgia or local surgical complications. Does the pain feel like an electric shock, and is there any visible redness, swelling, or drainage at the earring piercing sites? REQUEST TEST: Ear_Examination
